<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|340|THE ACTES|CHA. XVI.}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=16|verse=6}}† And passing through Phrygia and the countrie of Galatia, they vvere {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ This people had not the Gospel denied vnto them altogether, but for a time : because (as Venerable Bede thinketh) God foresavv they vvould not beleeue, & so should haue been more greuously damned.}}∷ forbidden by the holy Ghost to preach the vvord in Asia. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=7}}† And vvhen they vvere come into Mysia, they attempted to goe into Bithynia: and the Spirit of {{sc|Iesvs}} permitted them not.

{{verse|chapter=16|verse=8}}† And vvhen they had passed through Mysia, they vvent dovvne to Troas: {{verse|chapter=16|verse=9}}† and a vision by night vvas shevved to Paul: There vvas a certaine man of Macedónia standing and beseeching him, and saying, passe into Macedónia, and helpe vs. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=10}}† And as soone as he had seen the vision, forthvvith vve sought to goe into Macedónia, being assured that God had called vs to euangelize to them. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=11}}† And sailing from Troas, vve came vvith a straight course to Samothrácia, and the day folovving to Neapolis: {{verse|chapter=16|verse=12}}† and from thence to Philippi, vvhich is the first citie of the part of Macedonia, a {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''Colonia'', is such a citie vvhere the most inhabitants are strangers, sent thither from other great cities & States, namely from the Romanes.}}∷ ''colónia''. And vve were in this citie certaine daies, abiding. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=13}}† And vpon the day of the Sabboths, vve vvent forth vvithout the gate beside a riuer, vvhere it seemed that there vvas praier: & sitting vve spake to the vvomen that vvere assembled. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=14}}† And a certaine vvoman named Lydia, a seller of purple of the citie of the Thyatirians, one that vvorshipped God, did heare: vvhose hart our Lord opened to attend to those things vvhich vvere said of Paul. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=15}}† And vvhen she vvas baptized, and her house, she besought vs, saying: If you haue iudged me to be faithful to our Lord, enter in vnto my house, and tarie. And she constrained vs. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=16}}† And it came to passe as vve vvent to praier, a certaine vvenche hauing a Pythónical spirit, mette vs, that brought great gaine to her maisters by diuîning. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=17}}† This same folovving Paul and vs, cried saying, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Either the Diuel vvas compelled by the vertue of Paules presence to say truth, or els (as such do often times) he spake truth novv, that they might the more trust him, and he better beguile them at other times.}}∷ These men are the seruants of the high God, vvhich preach vnto you the vvay of saluation. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=18}}† And this she did many daies. And Paul being sorie, and turning, said to the spirit, I commaund thee in the name of {{sc|Iesvs Christ}} to goe out from her. And he vvent out the same houre. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=19}}† But her maisters seeing that the hope of their gaine vvas gone, apprehending Paul and Silas, brought them into the market place to the Princes: {{verse|chapter=16|verse=20}}† and presenting them to the magistrates, they said, These men trouble our citie, being Ievves: {{verse|chapter=16|verse=21}}† and they preach a fashion vvhich it is not lavvful for vs to receiue, nor doe, being Romanes. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=22}}† And the people ranne against them: and the magistrates tearing their coates, commaunded<noinclude>{{rh|||them}}</noinclude>
